conditions.manipulation_text: Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. A pressure-control malfunction led to rapid separator overpressure, a flammable-material release, personnel injuries, an oil spill, and production loss. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

surface_forms.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

case_payload.task: Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
case_payload.title: Comprehensive Node 1 HAZOP after a salient high-pressure incident vignette

surface_form_payload.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: The HAZOP evaluation systematically reviews Node 1 (separator V-001 and associated lines) across the six designated elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, and Start/Stop Procedures. Major process hazards include overpressure leading to containment loss, liquid carryover into fuel gas/burn pit headers, gas blowby to downstream equipment, and start-up errors involving bypass lines. Existing instrumentation and valves (PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101/102, SDV-101/102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103) mitigate several failure modes, but high/low safety trip interlocks and procedural enhancements are recommended.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Flow - Reverse: Reverse flow scenarios from the fuel gas system, burn pit, or Heater-Treater cannot be fully assessed because check valve locations and piping hydraulics are not specified in the packet.
Temperature - Less: Low temperature deviation is unresolved due to absence of minimum ambient temperature data and lack of cooling medium details in Node 1.
Fire/Explosion - External: External pool or jet fire impingement scenarios are unresolved due to lack of fireproofing, passive insulation, or deluge system data in the packet.

consequences: Vessel pressure exceeds nominal 60 psig and approaches design limits
Potential loss of containment or vessel overpressurization if relief capacity is exceeded
Hydrocarbon release with potential fire or explosion risk

evidence.relevance: Identifies Node 1 as separator V-001 and associated lines
Specifies nominal pressure of 60 psig and operating range up to 125 psig
Documents separated gas routing to fuel gas and burn pit
Identifies PV-101, PIT-101, PSV-101 A/B, and SDV-30010

possible_causes: Failure of PV-101 pressure control loop in the closed position
Blockage or restriction in separated gas line to fuel gas system or burn pit
Inlet gas surge exceeding normal separator handling capacity
recommendations: Verify that PSV-101 A/B relief sizing is sufficient for full blocked-outlet flow under maximum feed conditions
Implement high-pressure safety interlock on PIT-101 to close inlet SDV-30010 prior to PSV lift

consequences: Separator pressure drops below nominal 60 psig
Impaired three-phase separation efficiency of oil, water, and gas
Potential upset in gas fuel supply

evidence.relevance: Establishes nominal operating pressure of 60 psig
Lists PIT-101 and PV-101 as associated instrumentation

possible_causes: PV-101 pressure control valve failing fully open
Interruption of crude oil feed to V-001
Downstream header vacuum or sudden pull from fuel gas consumer
recommendations: Configure low-pressure alarm on PIT-101 in control room
Install minimum stop or low-pressure trip on PV-101 to prevent unmanaged depressurization

consequences: High liquid level in V-001 resulting in liquid carryover into the gas line
Contamination of fuel gas system and unburned liquid carryover into burn pit
Potential flameout, liquid spill, or fire hazard at burn pit

evidence.relevance: Identifies V-001 as three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator
Defines effluent routings to water treatment, burn pit/fuel gas, and Heater-Treater
Identifies LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, and SDV-30010

possible_causes: Failure of oil level control valve LV-101 or water level control valve LV-102 in closed position
Downstream line blockage in oily stream to Heater-Treater or water stream to water treatment
Severe inlet liquid surging
recommendations: Add high-level alarms for both oil and water compartments
Implement automated high-high level trip to close SDV-30010 on high liquid level

consequences: Loss of liquid seal inside separator V-001
Gas blowby into oily stream routing to downstream Heater-Treater
Gas blowby into water line routing to low-pressure water treatment facility causing downstream overpressure

evidence.relevance: Establishes density-based separation of gas, oil, and water in V-001
Identifies downstream Heater-Treater and Desalter train
Specifies water stream routing to water treatment
Identifies LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102

possible_causes: Failure of LV-101 or LV-102 in open position
Inlet feed interruption with liquid drain valves remaining throttled open
Level measurement failure
recommendations: Install independent low-low level interlocks configured to trip-close SDV-101 and SDV-102 upon loss of liquid seal
Assess downstream pressure ratings of water treatment and Heater-Treater under gas blowby conditions

consequences: Interruption of crude oil feed to V-001
Starvation and production loss in downstream Heater-Treater and V-003 Desalter

evidence.relevance: Traces continuous sequence V-001 to Heater-Treater to V-003 Electrostatic Desalter
Identifies E-001, FIT-101, FAL-103, and SDV-30010

possible_causes: Inadvertent or spurious closure of inlet SDV-30010
Upstream production shutdown or pipeline blockage
Severe scaling or fouling in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Ensure FAL-103 alarms in central control room to allow rapid diagnostic action before downstream heaters run dry
Verify SDV-30010 actuator health and test proof-test intervals

consequences: Operating temperature exceeds nominal 130 °F
Excessive light-ends vaporization inside V-001 leading to gas overloading
Thermal stress and potential degradation of internal/external vessel seals

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal temperature 130 °F and upper operating text limit 200 °F
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger in Node 1

existing_safeguards: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger design limits
possible_causes: Exchanger tube leak, heating medium regulator failure, or overfiring in upstream E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
Feed temperature excursion approaching 200 °F operating text limit
recommendations: Install continuous temperature indication and high-temperature alarm on V-001 inlet line downstream of E-001
Provide high-temperature cut-off on heating medium to E-001

consequences: Hydraulic transient, deadheading of upstream flow, or localized overpressure on separator inlet during start-up
Process disturbance and off-specification fluid discharge to downstream equipment

evidence.relevance: Lists Start/Stop Procedures as a required study element
Explicitly identifies source-supported procedural item regarding FWKO start-up without bypass opening

existing_safeguards: Standard operating procedures (noted in literature as historically lacking comprehensive human decision coverage)
possible_causes: Operator error during FWKO V-001 start-up sequence omitting bypass opening
Deficient or missing procedural steps for start-up bypass alignment in operating manual
recommendations: Revise and standardize FWKO start-up procedures to include a strict verification checkpoint for bypass valve opening
Implement valve status limit switches or mechanical interlocking to confirm bypass status during start-up

consequences: Thinning of vessel shell wall and nozzle necks in V-001
Loss of primary containment leading to sour fluid leakage, personnel hazard, or environmental release

evidence.relevance: Identifies V-001 as free water knock-out separator handling water phase separation
Shows separated water routed to water treatment
Lists Corrosion/Erosion as a source-study element

existing_safeguards: Corrosion allowance inherent in original vessel design specification
possible_causes: Continuous separation and accumulation of corrosive free water containing dissolved salts or acid gases
Erosive sand or particulate impingement in lower water boot and outlet nozzles
recommendations: Establish periodic non-destructive ultrasonic thickness testing program on lower shell and water outlet nozzles of V-001
Consider installation of corrosion coupons or sand probes in the aqueous separation zone

uncertainty_notes: PSV-101 A/B setpoints and relief capacity figures are not specified in the packet beyond operating range text (125 psig to 200 °F).
Piping layout, check valve presence, and downstream backpressures from the Heater-Treater and burn pit are not fully documented in the packet.
Organizational safety management practices are excluded from analysis in accordance with SYS-09.

[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.

[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
